name: AI Champions in Every Building
title: AI Champions in Every Building
answer: An AI champion in every building is a teacher who uses AI thoughtfully and helps colleagues nearby, so support is available where teachers work. The book treats this as shared leadership, because change spreads through people teachers trust. It matters because a champion can offer credible, local help, but only if the role is resourced and includes honest views about AI's limits.

sections.body: The idea is to place at least one AI champion in each school building. That person is a teacher who already uses AI with care and can assist colleagues, which makes help available in the place where teachers actually work. The book connects this to shared leadership, noting that change moves through trusted people rather than only through top-down policy. The problem it solves is that support can be distant or generic, while a colleague in the same building can respond to real classroom questions. It also aims for sound judgment rather than enthusiasm alone, so skeptical colleagues are not left out.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, a district or school identifies a teacher in each building who uses AI thoughtfully and can help others. The champion is not expected to add this work on top of a full teaching load, so the book says districts should provide release time, a small stipend, or reduced duties. Champions should also meet across buildings to share what they learn. The text does not give grade bands, so the arrangement is described for every building rather than for a particular age group. The champion's role is to support colleagues where they work, not to promote every AI tool.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels this as research. It states that research on principals spreading AI policy found that shared leadership was central to their approach, citing Avidov-Ungar & Ganon-Shilon, 2026. The book then reasons that champions are a form of shared leadership. No other study, figure, or finding is given in the supplied text. So the direct evidence is limited to that cited research, with the champion model presented as an application of it.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The main risk the book names is burnout. A champion who is asked to help colleagues while carrying a full teaching load will not be able to sustain the role, so release time, a small stipend, or reduced duties are needed. Another limit is credibility. A champion who is enthusiastic about everything may not help skeptical colleagues, while someone who is honest about AI's limits often has more credibility. The book says the aim is sound judgment, not promotional enthusiasm. The text does not say that champions hold formal decision rights over other teachers, so the role is described as support and shared leadership rather than authority.
